n-verdict.text:
Verdict system (one Muse Spark structured-output call per check)

PASS · teal · advance automatically, show next step
FAIL · coral · explain what is wrong, overlay SAM 3.1 mask on the part, offer reference photo
UNCLEAR · sky blue · ask for ONE specific extra photo (what + angle + distance). Never guess.
SAFETY GATE · amber shield · same loop, but only PASS unlocks the next step; no skip button.

Colors differ in lightness, not just hue, and every verdict also carries an icon + a word.

n-voice.text:
Hands-free rules

Mic is always on during a session (Muse Voice Transcribe realtime, ENDPOINTING mode, keywords = this skill's part names).

'done' / 'check' → capture + verify
'again' / 'repeat' → re-read the step
'what is this' → point-and-ask on current frame
'help' / 'I'm stuck' → escalate: text the author or find a pro

Every spoken reply is also printed in the sheet so the flow works muted.

n-glasses.text:
Lens card constraints (Device Access Toolkit)

· 600×600 private display, right lens. Phone serializes a FlexBox/Text/Image/Button/Icon layout and sends it over Bluetooth; each send replaces the whole card. Glasses hold no state.
· Keep a 48 px safe margin; one idea per card; ≥34 px text (it floats over the real world).
· Camera frames come from the glasses stream (720×1280 up to 30 fps) → phone → Muse Spark. Verify on 'done' or a Neural Band pinch.
· Audio: open-ear speakers read the instruction; mic feeds Voice Transcribe over normal Bluetooth.
· Non-Display glasses (Ray-Ban Meta Gen 2): same session, audio only, phone shows the card.
· Mock Device Kit simulates the camera path without hardware; the display needs real glasses.

n-modes.text:
How the three modes compare (no Meta model streams video; all three are request/response under the hood)

A · WATCH ME
Phone samples 1 low-res frame every 2 s and sends it with the running transcript; the guide may interject. Feels most like a video call. Latency to interject 3–5 s. Cost ≈ $0.03–0.05 per minute. Needs careful prompting so it stays quiet unless something is wrong. Hardest to build and to demo reliably.

B · SNAPSHOT CHECK
One full-res photo on 'done'; strict pass / fail / unclear verdict against the author's reference. Cheapest, most accurate, and it is the verification core every mode ends with. Not conversational on its own.

C · PUSH TO TALK
Tap: record voice + grab one frame. Tap: send. Reply arrives as text and speech, then the button is free again. One clear turn at a time, no accidental triggers, works in noisy kitchens, easiest to build. Latency 2–4 s per turn. Cost ≈ $0.01 per turn.

Recommendation: C as the default conversation mode, B as the step-verification call in every mode, A as an opt-in 'watch me' toggle on steps the author flags as error-prone. Build C + B first, add A if day 5 is free.

n-ptt-states.text:
Push-to-talk state machine (artboard C is live: press Play and tap the button)

IDLE → tap → RECORDING (video clip + mic, red frame; Voice Transcribe runs live so the transcript is ready the moment you stop)
RECORDING → tap → THINKING (mp4 clip uploaded to the Files API + transcript sent to Muse Spark in one request; button disabled)
THINKING → reply streams → ANSWERING (bubble + phone TTS, 'SPEAKING')
ANSWERING → speech ends → IDLE (transcript stays)

Layout: the feed is full screen. Chat lives in the bottom ~40% and is masked so bubbles fade to nothing just under mid-screen. Older turns scroll up into the fade. Cap clips at ~10 s (50 MB inline limit; longer goes via Files API).

The teal check button runs the strict snapshot verification (mode B) without leaving this screen.
